name: REF3030AIDBZR
title: REF30 and REF30E low-current series voltage references in SOT-23-3
summary: A family of three-pin series bandgap references in SOT-23. The REF30 comes in 1.25 V to 4.096 V with 0.2 % initial accuracy, 75 ppm/°C maximum drift, 42 µA quiescent current and 25 mA load current, and needs no output capacitor. The REF30E covers 1.25 V to 5 V with 0.1 % accuracy, 15 ppm/°C maximum drift, 27 µA quiescent current, and sources or sinks 10 mA. Both run from -40 °C to +125 °C; the REF3030AIDBZR is the 3.0 V REF30.
key_figures: 35 typ, 75 max ppm/°C (REF30); 5 typ, 15 max ppm/°C (REF30E)

circuits.title: Typical connections
circuits.description: The minimum hookup: supply into IN with a 0.1 µF bypass to ground, GND to ground, the reference taken from OUT. No output capacitor is needed for stability.

circuits.title: REF3025 with OPA703 giving +2.5 V and -2.5 V
circuits.description: A REF3025 on +5 V makes +2.5 V. An OPA703 on ±5 V inverts it with two equal 10 kΩ resistors: its non-inverting input is grounded, one resistor runs from +2.5 V to the inverting input and the other from the inverting input to the output, so the output sits at -2.5 V. The OPA703 has low offset voltage and low drift.

circuits.title: Basic data acquisition system 1 (REF3033 and ADS7822)
circuits.description: A REF3033 makes a 3.3 V rail that powers a microcontroller directly and, through a 5 Ω resistor, both the supply and the reference input of an ADS7822 ADC. Each side of the 5 Ω has a 1 µF to 10 µF capacitor to ground, and the ADC's reference pin has 0.1 µF more. The ADC's inverting input is grounded, its non-inverting input takes the signal, and its serial lines go to the microcontroller.

circuits.title: Basic data acquisition system 2 (REF3012 and ADS8324)
circuits.description: A 2.5 V supply feeds a REF3012, the microcontroller, and through a 5 Ω resistor the ADS8324's supply pin, with a 1 µF to 10 µF capacitor to ground on each side of the 5 Ω. The REF3012's 1.25 V output, bypassed with 0.1 µF, drives the ADC's reference input and its inverting input. The signal, 0 V to 1.25 V, enters the non-inverting input; the serial lines go to the microcontroller.

circuits.title: Low-power reference and bipolar input conditioning for a ΔΣ ADC
circuits.description: From a 3.3 V supply, a REF3030 makes a clean 3.0 V rail for the OPA317 and the REF3012, and the REF3012 makes 1.25 V for the ADC reference. The OPA317 attenuates a ±5 V input and shifts it up: R1 and R4 (100 kΩ) take the input pair to the two op-amp inputs, R2 (20 kΩ) pulls the non-inverting input toward 1.25 V and R3 (20 kΩ) toward ground, and R5 (10 kΩ) is the feedback. The output, centred on half the reference, passes an RC filter into the ADC's positive input. R6 and R7 (47 kΩ each) halve 1.25 V to 0.625 V, held by C2 (47 µF), for the ADC's negative input, so the ADC measures a differential signal within ±VREF/2.
notes: J1 pins 1 and 3 are the two sides of the positive input terminal, pins 2 and 4 of the negative one.

operation.text: A series bandgap reference. Two transistors run at different current densities; the difference of their base-emitter voltages rises with temperature and is placed across R1, amplified, and added to a base-emitter voltage that falls with temperature, so the sum holds nearly constant. The slight bow in output voltage across temperature comes from the base-emitter voltage's temperature coefficient not being quite linear.

Unloaded, the REF30 runs with its supply just 1 mV above the output, except the REF3012, which needs 1.8 V minimum. Its quiescent current is 42 µA typical at room temperature and 59 µA maximum over temperature, and moves less than 2.5 µA typical across the whole supply range. A supply below the specified minimum can make it draw more than its quiescent current for a moment; a supply that rises fast from a low impedance prevents this. The family is also specified to run from 50 mV above the output, with a supply bypass larger than 0.47 µF.
The shift in output voltage at 25 °C after the part has been taken through the full temperature range and back, in ppm of nominal output (equation VHYST).
Drift is measured by the box method. The REF30's typical drift is 20 ppm/°C over 0 °C to 70 °C and rises to 50 ppm/°C typical over -40 °C to +125 °C.

The REF30 has under 50 µVPP of noise from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz; noise grows with output voltage and with temperature. Extra filtering lowers it, provided the output impedance it adds does not spoil AC performance.
The REF30 output moves 24 ppm typical in the first 1000 hours and 15 ppm in the next 1000; the drift slows with time. The figures come from 30 units measured at regular intervals over 2000 hours.
Load regulation is the output change with load current. It is measured four-wire: separate force and sense lines meet at the output pin so contact and trace resistance do not add to the reading.

The REF30 is stable with no output capacitor. With a capacitive load, low-ESR, high-value capacitors need care, more so on low output voltages: on the REF3012 a low-ESR capacitor is kept to 10 µF or less. A 0.1 µF supply bypass is always used. The REF30E is specified stable from 0.1 µF to 22 µF of load capacitance with 10 mΩ to 500 mΩ ESR, and from 0.1 µF of input capacitance up.
With an OPA703 on ±5 V, a REF3025 gives both +2.5 V and -2.5 V (circuit split-reference).

Design targets: 3.3 V supply, ±5 V specified input, ±6 V maximum input, 1.25 V ADC reference. The ADC measures differentially; the op amp attenuates and shifts the ground-referenced input so its output centres on VREF/2 and swings within the ADC's ±VREF/2 range. The circuit still works, with lower accuracy, out to at least ±6 V, which eases overvoltage protection.

A low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass sits at the REF30's VIN. Other active parts get their own decoupling. A solid ground plane spreads heat and reduces EMI pickup. External parts sit close to the reference to avoid parasitic errors such as thermocouple (Seebeck) voltages. Traces from the reference to the INA and ADC bias connections are kept short. Sensitive analog traces do not run alongside digital ones; where they must cross, they cross at right angles.
